provenance.note: EVERY sentence in this file was invented for this measurement. No recording of anyone was consulted, no transcript of anyone appears, and no line here is a real spoken sentence. Every person, company, product and place name is fictional; the only non-fictional terms are `Deepgram`, `whisper.cpp`, `Postgres` and `MySQL`, which already appear in the public wiki as the doctrine's own worked examples.
provenance.shape: Utterances as whisper.cpp renders them: sentence case, punctuated, one to two sentences. `record` is the preceding exchange the utterance was said against, newest-last — Rich's line, or the CEO's own previous utterance as it was transcribed.
provenance.labels: `correction` = the CEO is fixing a word the machine got wrong, and a vocabulary entry is the right outcome. `not-a-correction` = anything else, including changes of mind, decisions between two real things, and ordinary prose that happens to contain the word `not`.
provenance.base rate: The negatives are ADVERSARIAL, not representative: 86 of 115 contain a standalone `not` pivot on purpose, which is far denser than real speech. Precision measured here is therefore a LOWER bound on precision in use, and recall is unaffected by the imbalance.
